Safeguarding
Everyone at Boundstone Nursery School works to help keep children safe from harm by providing a secure environment for children and their families.
Staff work closely with children and their families to build relationships, which result in a better ability to notice changes in behaviour and attitudes. With this knowledge we are able to provide support or take appropriate action to ensure all are kept safe, both at home and in the school.
The Designated Safeguarding Lead is Vikki Cripps, Head of School.
In her absence, the Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads are:
Our Safeguarding Team (ID 1445)
Vikki
Leonie
Carlie SENCo & Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead
Carlie
Debbie
Ruth
You can contact one of our Designated Safeguarding Leads at Boundstone Nursery School by calling 01903 276860.
If you have immediate concerns about a child’s safety you can contact Integrated Front Door on 01403 229 900 or out of hours on 0330 222 6664

Local Offer
Since September 2014, every Local Authority has been required to publish information about available services for children who have special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND). This is known as the ‘Local Offer’. This easy to understand information will set out what is normally available in schools and early years settings (e.g. playgroups and day nurseries) to support children with additional needs. It is not simply a list of services, but provides useful information on how to access services, any eligibility criteria, how decisions are made and who makes them.
Additionally, as a Maintained School we are required to publish further information in a SEND report which can be found below.
Please click below to read about our own offer for children with additional needs or to go to the West Sussex County Council Local Offer website

Curriculum & Ethos
We are a fully inclusive, free flow Nursery. This allows children to follow their own lead in their learning.
Jackie- Curriculum Lead
At Boundstone we encourage the children to take the lead in their learning by exploring, investigating and problem solving experiences.
We have enriching experiences that are linked to the Early Years Foundation Stage, to give children the ability to build on their knowledge, and to collaborate with others.
We have a continuous provision that allows children to be independent and enables them to take their learning forward.

Bank Staff Assistant Childcare Worker - Nursery/Daycare
Accountable to: Senior Childcare Worker/Teacher/Nursery Manager/ Daycare Manager
Accountable for: None
Purpose
To work as an enthusiastic, motivated and committed team member in Boundstone Nursery School, providing an inclusive, caring and stimulating environment with exciting opportunities that meet all children’s developmental needs and interests.
Key Tasks and Duties
The specific accountabilities of this flexible role may alter from time to time in order to meet the needs of the business/client, but accountabilities will include (or be equivalent in nature to) those listed below:
• Remain up to date and compliant with all relevant legislation, organisational procedures, policies and professional codes of conduct in order to uphold standards of best practice.

Person Specification
This section outlines the key criteria that must be addressed when submitting an application for employment as shortlisting for interview will be based on information supplied here.
Level of Knowledge
Knowledge of working with young children.
Qualifications and Professional Membership
A commitment to personal and professional development.
Experience
• Experience of working with young children or in a relevant setting.
Skills
Competencies
Location
Boundstone Nursery SchoolUpper Boundstone LaneLancingWest SussexBN15 9QX

If you're ready to make a positive impact in the lives of young children and play a vital role in their development, we'd love to hear from you!

Links to useful SEND services
The links below are useful organisations, to support families :
Reaching Families is a parent-carer led, grassroots charity which aims to support parents and families of children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) in their daily lives, in particular through the delivery of information, training and peer support.
We offer full-time, term-based provision, either in-person at Centres or at Red Balloon of the Air, which offers a hybrid of online and face-to-face support (up to 15 hours per week).
Our approach puts wellbeing at the core of our students’ education experience, with a strong emphasis on mental health, personal development and positive social interaction alongside academic teaching.
We’re a clinician-led company that believes Autism and ADHD assessments should always be carried out in-person and to a high standard.
At Aspens we provide high quality care and support to people on the autism spectrum and with learning disabilities; and their families; meeting their needs and aspirations and empowering them to learn and grow through an integrated network of services across the South-East.
We help families in Sussex to overcome their difficulties and prevent crisis. We support families struggling with issues such as poverty, ill health, learning difficulties, bereavement, family break-up and domestic abuse.
WSPCF is an independent charity for the parent carers of children and young people aged 0-25 with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND).
We support parent carers by providing information, signposting, and training that equips them in their lifelong caring role and empowers them to participate in shaping services for their children and young people.
These bitesize videos have been produced by West Sussex Educational Psychology (EP) Service to inform and support the practice of adults working with children and young people in educational settings.
They are designed to provide the key information and practical strategies necessary to effectively support the young people you are working with. These webinars may be of particular use if you have attended a consultation or received advice from an EP in supporting you or the staff at your setting in implementing EP recommendations.
Educational Psychology Service
A national, award-winning charity empowering the nation to sleep better
We are one of the leading, independent expert voices on sleep issues in the UK and we are here to help everyone get a better night’s sleep. Whether it’s advice, education or support for children, teenagers, adults, workplaces or professionals, we are on hand with expert knowledge, resources and accredited training.
It’s time to wake up to sleep.

Fees
We understand that choosing the right nursery is an important decision for your family, and clarity around fees is a key part of that process.
At Boundstone Nursery School, our fees reflect the high quality of care, education, and nurturing environment we provide for every child. They cover our experienced staff, carefully planned learning activities, and the resources that support your child’s development during their time with us.
Below you’ll find clear information about our session fees and any additional costs. If you have any questions or would like help understanding your childcare funding entitlement, we will be happy to assist. Please note we are a term time only provider.
Morning Session - 9am-12pm
Packed lunch - £5.50
Afternoon Session - 1pm-4pm
After School Session-
3pm-4pm (only applies to children attending a ‘long’ 9am-3pm day)
Government Funded Hours (From 9 Months)
Boundstone Nursery School is pleased to offer Government-funded childcare for eligible children from 9 months of age, helping families access high-quality early education from the very start of their child’s learning journey.
From the term after your child turns 9 months, eligible working families may be able to access 30 hours of funded childcare, depending on their circumstances. Funded hours are available during term time and can be used across a pattern of sessions, subject to availability. While the funding covers the cost of early education, additional charges may apply for hot meals or hours taken beyond the funded entitlement.
We are happy to guide you through the eligibility and application process, and answer any questions you may have, about how funded hours can be used at Boundstone Nursery School. If you require more information on your entitlement, visit the Childcare choices tab below , or the Admissions tab to contact Admissions directly.

pageCache.text:
Using fresh and locally sourced ingredients, Little Tums offer a 3-week rolling menu, which doesn’t just offer a great variety of food but also meets the “Healthy Choice Award” guidelines that have been set out to the highest standard. Their menu plan has been awarded the highest Gold accreditation by being fully compliant with the recommended GDA’s and dietary requirements for children of nursery and school age.
The menus are designed in-house by a team of qualified chefs and then independently evaluated to ensure they meet the daily nutritional guidelines. Therefore, each child that receives a Little Tums meal is being provided a healthy, balanced and nutritious meal.
All children can access hot lunches, these are charged at £4.50 per meal. If you believe you are entitled to free school meals, please visit the Free School Meals section to apply.
Hot lunches
Little Tums' homemade hot lunches are all prepared on the day they are to be served, this ensure that each meal that is prepared, only contains ingredients that are fresh and tasty, ensuring quality and consistency throughout the meals.
Special dietary and cultural meals, make up a large percentage of the meals we prepare daily. Much care is taken into ensuring that they are prepared, in line with the children’s requirements. The dietary chefs take great pride in ensuring that their meals, are just as nutritionally balanced and tasty and therefore enjoyed. It is important that each child, regardless of their dietary, allergen or cultural needs has access to meals that are as similar as possible to our main menu.
All hot food is cooked to a minimum of 85 degrees centigrade, and once this minimum temperature is reached, the meals are packed into gastronorm containers. These are then sealed and labelled with the nursery name and allergen information. These are then packaged into hot holding thermo boxes which ensure your meals remain hot through transportation and arrive to you hot and ready to serve.

Makaton Signing
At Boundstone Nursery School, we use Makaton signing to support communication and inclusion for all children. By combining simple signs with spoken words, Makaton helps children express themselves, build confidence, and develop language skills. Our staff use Makaton naturally throughout the day, creating a supportive environment where every child feels heard, understood, and included. You can support your child by practising the signs at home. To help you can download our Makaton guide below :
Tiny Happy People can help you develop your child’s language and communication skills, so they get the best start in life. Please visit the website for more information.

How do we support our families ...
We pride ourselves on the level of support we provide to our SEND children and their families. We run a number of support and information sessions, which you would be most welcome to attend. Details of the current groups can be found below :
SEND Stay & Play
Stay and play weekly sessions for children aged 2-5 with special educational needs and disabilities and their parents.
This is a great opportunity for children with additional needs to play, get messy and busy in a safe environment and for parents/carers to network with each other and get support from our expert Play and Learn Coordinator, Donna.
When? Every Wednesday afternoon from 2.00pm-3.30pm Term time only
Where? Boundstone Nursery School
Please email Donna Brigden for more information and to book a space : donna.brigden@westsussex.gov.uk
Spaces are limited so book early
Sessions are free
Siblings welcome – please confirm with Donna
Family Support Work Drop - In
Every 2 weeks, the charity "Family Support Work" will join us to offer support, guidance and signposting of information for families. Tea, coffee and cake are provided. If you would like more information please contact :
Stacey 07545 092814 or Becca 07747 481360
